AI and tensors

Small CPU-only programs demonstrate tensor arithmetic and a trainable XOR model.

examples/tensors.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 8b7195600c448d89

// Differentiable computation in PEACOCK: matmul, loss, reverse-mode gradients.
module tensors

use nn

fn main() -> Unit {
    capability compute;

    let x = tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]);
    let column = tensor([[0.5], [1.5]]);
    let projected = x.matmul(column);
    print("matmul: " + str(projected));
    print("shape: " + str(projected.shape));
    print("softmax: " + str(tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]]).softmax()));

    let weights = nn.parameter([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.4]]);
    let targets = tensor([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]);
    let predictions = x.matmul(weights);
    let loss = nn.mse(predictions, targets);
    print("loss: " + str(loss.item()));
    loss.backward();
    print("weight gradient: " + str(weights.grad));

    // Analytic check: for mean-squared error, dL/dW = X^T * (2/N) * (P - T).
    let expected = x.transpose().matmul((predictions - targets) * 0.5);
    print("autodiff gradient: " + str(weights.grad));
    print("closed-form gradient: " + str(expected));
    print("max abs difference: " + str(nn.max_abs_diff(weights.grad, expected)));
}

examples/xor.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 1af124d491c4d489

// Train a small neural network on XOR, entirely through PEACOCK syntax.
module xor_net

use nn

model XorNet {
    input x: Tensor<Float32, [2]>
    output y: Tensor<Float32, [2]>
    stack {
        Dense(units: 8, activation: relu)
        Dense(units: 2)
    }
}

training XorTraining {
    objective: "cross_entropy"
    optimiser: "adam"
    epochs: 400
    learning_rate: 0.05
    batch_size: 4
    seed: 7
}

fn main() -> Unit {
    capability compute;
    let data = nn.xor();
    let net = XorNet.init(seed: 7);
    let losses = XorTraining.run(net, data);
    let accuracy = XorTraining.evaluate(net, data);
    print("epochs: " + str(len(losses)));
    print("final loss: " + str(nn.loss(net, data, loss: "cross_entropy")));
    print("accuracy: " + str(accuracy));
}

Run the training example with `./bin/peacock run examples/xor.pac --grant compute`. No GPU is required or claimed.

Graphics

The reference renderer can produce deterministic image output from PEACOCK programs.

examples/aurora.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 826d859a751e4f4f

// Deterministic procedural colour: render an aurora to a real PNG.
module aurora

use colour
use graphics

fn main() -> Unit {
    capability fs;
    let canvas = graphics.canvas(960, 540);
    let palette = [
        colour.oklch(0.55, 0.18, 160.0),
        colour.oklch(0.72, 0.20, 285.0),
        colour.oklch(0.62, 0.16, 60.0)
    ];
    graphics.gradient(canvas, palette, 35.0);
    graphics.aurora(canvas, 1.5, 42);
    graphics.save(canvas, "examples/out/aurora.png");
    print("wrote examples/out/aurora.png");
}

The current renderer is software 2D; aurora colour fields are artistic procedural graphics, not a physical sky simulation.
